_doc: Polish toggle semantics shared by both engines. mode_toggles is used when no custom prompt is sent; mode_custom replaces it when custom_prompt is present (the toggles are then ignored, as in the original app where instruction becomes custom_prompt: ...). Placeholders in polish-system.txt: {{MODE}} {{RULES}} {{VOICE}}. Unknown custom toggle labels are appended verbatim as an extra rule. The toggle label 'Prompt Engineer' (sent by the built-in transform as a custom toggle) maps to the prompt_engineer rule.
mode_toggles: Apply exactly the rules listed below, and only those. Rules that are not listed must not be applied.
mode_custom: Apply the user prompt below to the text. It replaces any default polishing rules; follow it exactly and change nothing else.

toggles.Make more concise: Make it more concise: cut filler, repetition, hedging and words that add nothing, without dropping any point.
toggles.Reword for clarity: Reword for clarity: replace vague, clumsy or ambiguous phrasing with plain, precise wording.
toggles.Reorder for readability: Reorder for readability: move sentences or ideas so the text flows logically, context first and conclusions after.
toggles.Add structure for readability: Add structure for readability: split long blocks into short paragraphs, and turn enumerations of three or more parallel items into a list.
toggles.Maintain your tone: Maintain the tone: keep the register, warmth and personality of the original wording; do not make it stiffer or more casual.
toggles.Clarify main point: Clarify the main point: make the central message or request unmistakable, stating it early.
toggles.Refine phrasing for impact: Refine phrasing for impact: use stronger, more vivid and more direct wording and active verbs.
toggles.Prompt Engineer:
Turn the text into a clean, optimized prompt for an AI assistant. The text is messy, spoken, unstructured thoughts: infer the role, task, context, inputs, output requirements and constraints from it, and do not answer the prompt. Write the prompt in exactly this structure, keeping the bold headings, and leave a section out only when the text gives nothing for it. Put placeholders in square brackets where the text implies a value it does not state. Never add requirements the text does not imply.

**Title**
(1 concise line)

**Role & stance**
(who the model is and how it should behave)

**Task**
(what the model must do)

**Context**
(only what the model needs to know)

**Inputs available**
(explicit list)

**Output requirements**
(format, structure, tone, length, only if specified; otherwise placeholders)

**Constraints / Do-nots**
(bulleted)

**Examples / References**
(include all examples verbatim)

**Execution checklist**
(short, factual verification list)

**Conflict resolution**
(only if applicable)
